shared_elements: carved pale stone surface in low relief
horizontal band/register of repeated small motifs
weathered, outdoor stone surface with damage and chipping
justification: Both are weathered pale stone surfaces organised with at least one horizontal band of repeated small motifs, and both include profile bird-like forms and small disc shapes, which is the most specific correspondence. However, A is a flat wall covered edge-to-edge with dense rows of tiny sunken-relief signs of uniform scale, whereas B is a free-standing shaped pillar bearing a few large, boldly modelled raised-relief animal figures, so the manner of carving and the compositional logic differ fundamentally.
